name: create_c_linked_list
description: Creates a singly linked list of ints in C with insert/delete/find/print commands
prompts:
Create a C program in a file called linked_list.c that implements a singly linked list of ints, using a struct `Node` with an int `value` field and a `struct Node *next` field, and a single global head pointer that starts as NULL. The program's main() must read commands from stdin, one per line, until end-of-input (EOF), and for each command produce the following behavior:
- `insert X` - insert integer X at the HEAD of the list. Produce no output.
- `delete X` - remove the first node in the list whose value equals X (if any); if no node has that value, do nothing. Produce no output.
- `find X` - print `1` on its own line if a node with value X exists in the list, otherwise print `0` on its own line.
- `print` - print all values currently in the list from head to tail, space-separated, on one line (an empty line if the list is empty).
Each command and its integer argument (if any) are whitespace-separated on their own line.

test_setup_files.test_linked_list.py:
import subprocess
subprocess.run(['gcc', 'linked_list.c', '-o', 'linked_list_bin'], check=True)

commands = '\n'.join([
    'insert 1',
    'insert 2',
    'insert 3',
    'print',
    'find 2',
    'find 5',
    'delete 2',
    'print',
    'find 2',
]) + '\n'

proc = subprocess.run(['./linked_list_bin'], input=commands, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
assert proc.returncode == 0, f'nonzero exit: {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr[-300:]}'
lines = [l.strip() for l in proc.stdout.strip('\n').split('\n')]
assert lines[0] == '3 2 1', f'expected head-first order "3 2 1", got {lines[0]!r} (full output: {proc.stdout!r})'
assert lines[1] == '1', f'expected find 2 -> 1, got {lines[1]!r}'
assert lines[2] == '0', f'expected find 5 -> 0, got {lines[2]!r}'
assert lines[3] == '3 1', f'expected print after delete -> "3 1", got {lines[3]!r}'
assert lines[4] == '0', f'expected find 2 -> 0 after delete, got {lines[4]!r}'
print('PASS')
